subject: Rollout lifecycle handoff and doc-gap questions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rollout lifecycle handoff and doc-gap questions

Team — looping you together to confirm the handoff cadence for the upcoming Acme integration (target release week of Nov 30). There are three interlocking items I want to align on:

1) Release timing: product has flagged a potential scope tweak that might push the go-live by ~1 week. Aditya, can you confirm whether the change is on the critical path for rollout? If so we need an explicit canary plan and rollback trigger.
2) Enablement docs: Kimberly, we need a stripped-down playbook for CS and Solutions (preflight checklist + troubleshooting ladder). A one‑pager + slides would be ideal.
3) Exceptions and routing: Vivek — if we hit a security gating exception (S3 permission audit), what is the fastest internal path to approve a temporary exception and who signs?

Attached a draft set of slides and the current canary matrix (very rough) — please update the matrix with owners per lane. I’d like a firm plan by EOD Tuesday so the GTM kickoff can proceed Wednesday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Program Ops, Redwood Inference
415-555-0187
attachments: redwood_enablement_slides_v1.pdf, canary_rollout_matrix.xlsx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rollout lifecycle handoff and doc-gap questions

Hannah — quick update from Product/Release: the scope tweak is a runtime config change to default batching thresholds (not a model or infra change). We're not blocked, but it does affect latency baselines that Acme cares about.

Plan:
- We can keep Nov 30 as GA if we push the config change into a canary for two weekdays and validate latency and error rates.
- Rollback trigger: if tail latency (p95) increases >20% or error rate delta >0.5% over baseline during canary windows.
- Owner: Aditya (canary), Marissa (test validation), Vivek (exception routing).

I'll update the canary matrix with owner columns and add the specific telemetry checks.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rollout lifecycle handoff and doc-gap questions

Thanks — clarifying the exception path:
- For security gating exceptions (S3, KMS, network policy), the fastest path is a scoped temporary exception signed by Security (if <48 hours) plus one Platform/Infra lead. If >48 hours it needs a Risk review and an exec sponsor.
- For Acme specifically, since this is an enterprise tenant with a signed DPA, we can do a 24–48 hour scoped exception with Security + Infra approval.

Action: Kimberly, can you add an "exception contact card" to the playbook with phone/Slack pings for Security and Infra, and a template approval note?

Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability & SRE
From: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rollout lifecycle handoff and doc-gap questions

Hannah — thanks for the heads up. A few constraints from Acme:
- We need a documented SLA for latency (target p95 under 400ms for standard requests).
- During canary we cannot route >5% of production traffic without a signed exception.
- The procurement team needs a single point-of-contact for post-GA support (preferably a named Solutions Engineer).

If you can confirm the canary windows and the named SE by Tuesday EOD, we’ll be able to keep Nov 30.

Jenna Liu
Senior PM, Acme Corp
jenna.liu@acme-corp.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@acme-corp.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rollout lifecycle handoff and doc-gap questions

All — consolidated update and action items:

Decision: Keep Nov 30 GA with a 3-day canary starting Nov 23 (Tue–Thu) with progressive traffic ramps (1% day 1, 3% day 2, 5% day 3).

Owners and deliverables by EOD Tuesday (Nov 11):
- Aditya: finalize canary telemetry checks and populate canary matrix (JIRA: RINF-4387).
- Marissa: build quick validation runbook for test/QA + signoff checklist.
- Kimberly: produce a 1-page playbook (preflight checklist + exception contact card) and a 10-slide enablement deck for Solutions/SEs. Attach to Drive folder.
- Vivek: confirm exception approval flow and provide a template approval note.
- Hannah: coordinate GTM kickoff and publish final timeline.

Acme asks noted: p95 latency SLA and SE point-of-contact. Marissa — can you propose a named SE for Acme? If not, Kimberly please list the rotation and on-call window.

I'll update the Drive with the revised matrix and circulate the final slide link after EOD Tuesday.

Thanks everyone — quick wins keep this on track.

Hannah
Head of Program Ops, Redwood Inference
attachments: updated_canary_matrix.xlsx (in Drive)
